issues.description: revoke_error exposed without classification of what the value actually is
issues.detail: The PR author flagged the concern themselves: is it safe to display the revoke error? That question is the entire job here. RevokeErr is a string carrying internal failure context; it complects 'operator diagnostic' with 'API response field'. Decide which one it is, document the contract, and redact if the answer is the former.

issues.description: leaseInfoForExport reaches into unexported namespace field, complecting value-copy with identity
issues.detail: The export struct now carries `namespace`, an unexported pointer to a mutable namespace identity, alongside immutable time/path values. The exported leaseEntry is no longer a clean value snapshot; callers can observe namespace mutation through a 'redacted' copy. Either copy namespace.Path as a plain string, or document that this is a reference, not a value.

issues.description: function renamed but metric label and old name still leak through
issues.detail: FetchLeaseInfo still emits the metric `expire.fetch-lease-times` and the test `TestExpiration_FetchLeaseTimesIrrevocable` keeps the old name. The rename was meant to signal that this returns more than times; leaving the old identifiers scattered re-complects the two meanings the rename was trying to separate.

issues.description: response shape complects 'field absent' with 'field empty' inconsistently
issues.detail: `path` is always set; `namespace_path` and `revoke_error` are conditionally omitted when empty; `expire_time` is set to nil then overwritten. Three different absence conventions in one response map. Pick one: always-present-with-zero-value, or omit-when-empty. Clients now have to know per-field which rule applies.

issues.description: test asserts one new field; namespace_path and revoke_error have no coverage
issues.detail: The added test checks `path == "secret/foo"` and nothing else. The two more interesting additions — conditional namespace_path emission and the security-sensitive revoke_error — are untested. Tests should cover the behavior that actually carries risk, not the easy field.

review.summary: The change is a reasonable widening of a value export, but it ships with the author's own unanswered security question still in the PR body — that question is the design decision, not a footnote. The deeper issue is mild complecting: leaseInfoForExport now mixes immutable times and paths with a live reference to a namespace identity, and the response map uses three different conventions for absent fields. The rename from FetchLeaseTimes to FetchLeaseInfo is the right instinct but only half-applied; the metric name and a test name still carry the old meaning. Decide what revoke_error is (operator diagnostic vs API contract), make the response shape uniform, and either copy namespace.Path as a value or be explicit that a reference crosses the boundary.
